events.text: In 2023, Jollibee Foods completed a corporate carbon footprint assessment and publicly disclosed its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions according to the GHG Protocol, covering Scope 1 and Scope 2.
In 2022, Jollibee's scope 1 emissions were 46,295.9 tons of CO2e and scope 2 emissions were 440,564.15 tons CO2e.
The Jollibee Group's 2024 sustainability report reports 31,339 employees, 29.6 average training hours per employee, and 16,800 solar panels generating 9.1 megawatts of clean energy.
In 2023, Jollibee Foods Corporation conducted over 15,600 Food Safety audits globally, achieving a 7-star rating for exceptional Food Safety and Quality Practices.
Jollibee Group's third manufacturing facility, Jollibee Worldwide Services-Logistics, incorporated renewable energy.
Jollibee Group switched on 99% renewable electricity to power its commissaries in the Philippines, enabled through renewable electricity from First Gen.
Jollibee Group completed installation of more than 16,800 rooftop solar panels across four facilities in the Philippines, delivering 9.1 megawatts of renewable energy capacity.
Jollibee Foods Corp. faced backlash for firing workers seeking better pay, amid allegations of worker exploitation.
In 2018, the Philippines' Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) said Jollibee Foods Corp. topped the list of companies with the most contractual employees.
